title: My Hero Academia Creator Returns to Shonen Jump After 2 Years With New Horror Manga
content: My Hero Academia ‘s creator has returned to the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine two years after its finale with a brand new Horror inspired manga. Kohei Horikoshi has been moving on from the hero series for the past couple of years as the manga officially ended its story with a few epilogue entries…
author: ComicBook

title: 13 Years Later, Major Fantasy Anime Confirms Big Upgrade for 2026 Revival
content: Puella Magi Madoka Magica is making its return with a brand new feature film release 13 years after it last hit the big screen, and its new movie comeback has revealed it will be getting a big upgrade for its launch in theaters later this Summer.
author: ComicBook

title: Dragon Ball Super Artist Honors the Year’s Biggest Isekai With Special Makeover
content: Dragon Ball Super ‘s artist has made a comeback to help celebrate the biggest Isekai anime franchise of the year, and it has resulted in some cool new art giving the franchise a fresh makeover.
author: ComicBook

title: Manga 'Gabriel DropOut' Concludes Serialization
content: The official X account for author Ukami announced on Sunday that the Gabriel DropOut manga will end in the October issue of Comic Dengeki Daioh "g" magazine, marking the end of the manga's nearly 13-year run. Ukami began serializing the supernatural comedy manga in Comic Dengeki Daioh "g" magazine in December 2013.
author: MyAnimeList

title: Villains Are Destined to Die Webtoon TV Anime Adaptation Announced as Main Story Ends
content: The popular Korean webtoon Villains Are Destined to Die is officially getting a TV anime adaptation. The announcement comes alongside the completion of the webtoon’s main story, which concluded with Chapter 214. No information about the TV anime’s studio, staff, cast, release window, or format has been announced.
author: Anime Corner

title: Villains Are Destined to Die Webtoon Ends, Gets TV Anime
